title: Sweatman's three clarinets and two Boston jobs
summary: He mentions Wilbur Sweatman's three-clarinet act and his two daily Boston jobs, a lunch restaurant and a dance, where gambling cost him his pay.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: And I had another guy, I can't think of his name.
Did you ever know Cliff King and Wilbur Sweatman? They used to do that thing.

Well, Sweatman used to play three clarinets, played a -- Mother Machree, I think it was. He used to play something where he'd used three clarinets. And at this job, I used to go in there and they had 12:00 over there, at Beach Street and that was a restaurant where all the secretaries would come in for lunch. And we used to play from 12:00 to 2:00.

Yeah, and then go back there at 12:00 at night, play for the dancers. Here I had two jobs and never made a nickel. I'd have to go to one job and collect some money and go to the next job and pay off. I was gambling, that's when I was gambling.
